Is an object the output of a mapper function?

Source: R/data-frame-predicates.R
data-frame-predicates.Rd

  • is_map_df() tests whether an object is the output of a mapper of any tier, i.e., of a function made by function_map(), function_map_seq(), or function_map_total_n(), such as grim_map().

  • is_map_basic_df(), is_map_seq_df(), and is_map_total_n_df() test for one tier each.

Usage

is_map_df(x)

is_map_basic_df(x)

is_map_seq_df(x)

is_map_total_n_df(x)

Arguments

x

Object to be tested.

Value

Logical (length 1).

Details

See vignette("consistency-tests-in-depth") for the three tiers and the table at its end.

Examples

df1 <- pigs1 |>
  grim_map(digits_x = 2, items_averaged = 1, data_type = "integer")
df2 <- pigs1 |>
  grim_map_seq(digits_x = 2, items_averaged = 1, data_type = "integer")
df3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x1,  ~x2,  ~n,
  3.43, 5.28, 90,
  2.97, 4.42, 103
) |>
  grim_map_total_n(digits_x = 2, items_averaged = 1, data_type = "integer")

# All three are mapper output:
is_map_df(df1)
#> [1] TRUE
is_map_df(df2)
#> [1] TRUE
is_map_df(df3)
#> [1] TRUE

# Each is the output of one tier:
is_map_basic_df(df1)
#> [1] TRUE
is_map_seq_df(df2)
#> [1] TRUE
is_map_total_n_df(df3)
#> [1] TRUE

is_map_basic_df(df2)
#> [1] FALSE
is_map_seq_df(df3)
#> [1] FALSE
